issues.description: getCategoryLabel complects a lookup table with three different heuristics in one function
issues.detail: The old code was a plain data map from id to label. The new code drops the data and infers labels via 'special cases', then a regex for version suffixes, then a length check, then default casing. Four rules braided into one function to replace a hashmap. Keep the data: ship an explicit id->label map and fall back to a tiny formatter only for unknowns.

issues.description: Length-<=3 heuristic will mislabel real category words as acronyms
issues.detail: 'iam' becoming 'IAM' is correct by accident; any future 3-letter category like 'web', 'log', or 'key' will render as 'WEB', 'LOG', 'KEY'. The rule encodes a guess about the world rather than a fact. The previous CATEGORY_LABELS map stated facts; this function states a hope. Restore the data table and let the formatter handle only truly unknown ids.

issues.description: selectedPoint is overloaded as both 'detail panel target' and 'radar fade state'
issues.detail: handleCategoryChange and handlePointClick both write the same selectedPoint, and CustomDot reads it to decide fade. One identity now carries two distinct meanings: 'which row is shown in the details panel' and 'which dot the radar is highlighting'. They happen to coincide today; the moment a designer wants 'highlight without opening the panel' they diverge. Separate the two values.

issues.description: SEVERITY_ORDER aliases two keys to value 4, hiding identity-vs-value confusion
issues.detail: Adding Info: 4 alongside Informational: 4 papers over an upstream naming inconsistency rather than naming it. The map now answers 'what rank is this string' for two strings that mean the same thing, with no record of which is canonical. Normalize severity strings at the edge and keep one key per rank.

issues.description: HorizontalBarChart recomputes maxValue and percentage inside the row render
issues.detail: calculatedWidth and displayPercentage are functions of the whole data array but live inside the .map callback, so maxValue is recomputed per row and item.percentage is treated as authoritative in one branch and ignored in another. Compute the derived values once above the loop and pass plain {width, label} values into the row. Pure function over data, called once.

issues.description: 'Prowler ThreatScore' rename is a naming concern braided into a feature PR
issues.detail: The Risk Radar feature is one concern; renaming 'Threat Score' to 'Prowler ThreatScore' across tooltips, axes, card titles, and delta copy is a separate concern about product vocabulary. Bundling them means any future revert of the rename drags the radar with it. Not blocking, but worth splitting next time so each change has one reason to exist.

review.summary: The PR ships a working radar view, but trades a small data table (CATEGORY_LABELS) for a four-rule heuristic function and calls the result "shared utilities." That is easy, not simple: the old code stated facts; the new code guesses. The radar client also complects "selected for details panel" and "selected for fade highlight" into one identity, and HorizontalBarChart computes whole-dataset aggregates inside a per-row map. None of this blocks merge, but the category label change is one CATEGORY_LABELS map away from being genuinely simple — the question that should have been asked first is "why are we replacing data with rules?"
